text:
arjun: Heads up — console charts are janky after the frontend deploy. When I switch time ranges the whole chart freezes for ~2-3s :grimacing:
lucy: saw a bunch of complaints in #support a few mins ago, and bundle size on master jumped ~120KB gzipped compared to last week :eyes:
ben: can repro locally. profiler shows a big parse/eval spike in main.chunk.js around startup, not just rendering.
console-bot: deploy finished: frontend@2026.03.18-rc3 -> prod (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:
arjun: telemetry (client perf) points to a parse+compile hit where the locale payloads get evaluated. stack trace points to an Intl polyfill/locale import inside the charting wrapper. snippet:```js
// bad: landed in main bundle
import 'intl-locales-supported';
import 'react-intl/locale-data/en';
```
lucy: wait we specifically made locales dynamic to keep main small. how did this land in main?
ben: looks like the charting lib does a top-level require for locale detection during module init, so webpack included it in the main graph. dynamic import rules got flattened because of a transitive sync import.
arjun: that explains the parse spike + the freeze on range switch (chart init triggers extra sync work). also seeing heavy main-thread work from d3 update loops while the big chunk is parsed — double whammy.
lucy: short-term mitigation options? canary revert? lazy-load locales after paint? preload chunk?
ben: pragmatic plan: 1) revert the locale import to explicit dynamic import so it doesn't get hoisted, 2) add requestIdleCallback fallback to load locales after first paint, 3) add a temporary server-side header to allow chunk caching aggressively.
arjun: agree. example patch to lazy-load:```js
// in chart-wrapper init
if (!window.Intl || !areLocalesLoaded()) {
  requestIdleCallback(() => import(/* webpackChunkName: "locales" */ './locales').then(initLocales));
}
```
lucy: can we also change the rollout UX so we can push this fix to only 10% of users immediately? I want to validate perf before full rollout.
ben: deploy tooling supports percent rollouts, but it's per-service not per-route. that's been painful for console routes — we should file an infra item to support route-scoped rollouts. for now we can do canary cluster -> 10%.
arjun: I'll open a quick PR to revert the bad import and include the idle-callback load, push to canary. ben, can you add a webpack config tweak to ensure the locales chunk is separate (splitChunks manual entry)? lucy, will you watch telemetry for canary?
ben: on it. locally testing with `yarn build:dev && node serve-dist` — repro steps in the gist.
ben: repro command:```bash
# run build and serve locally
yarn build:local && npx serve dist
# open http://localhost:5000/console -> switch time range -> profile
```
deploy-bot: starting canary rollout: frontend-canary -> 10% of traffic :beach_umbrella:
arjun: thanks. lucy please add a short perf panel to the console dashboard (time-to-first-paint, main-parse-time, long-task count) so we can see impact. add a tracing hook if possible. :mag:
lucy: will do, adding a perf trace and alert threshold. ping me if canary is live so I can watch graphs.
arjun: assigning: @lucy -> canary telemetry/watch, @ben -> webpack chunk/split and local repro, @arjun -> quick lazy-load PR. target to merge in 30m and roll to 10%.
lucy: ack. I'll also post a short note to #support with a status update. :thumbsup:
arjun: if canary looks good we'll ramp. if not, revert and ship hotfix.
ben: one more note — long-term we should audit any third-party libs doing sync locale detection during module init. that's been a recurring footgun. filing a follow-up ticket.
arjun: thanks team. I'll post the PR link in this thread in a few mins.
